HOW TO READ THIS CHAPTER

Scope, sources & credits

The study list

We selected globally assessed Animalia entries classified as Vulnerable, Endangered or Critically Endangered in IUCN 2026-1, then checked marine identity and accepted names against WoRMS. The list contains 1,608 IUCN entries, corresponding to 1,601 accepted WoRMS taxon IDs. It is a project study list, not a complete global census.

Twelve entries have ambiguous taxonomic links. After excluding them, 1,596 entries remained eligible for matching to CITES data. We found at least one record for 387 entries in the study period.

Reading the charts

Gold, copper and coral mark Vulnerable, Endangered and Critically Endangered. In the square charts, lighter shades mean more study entries. Each chart uses one count scale across its risk groups.

The class charts compare all study entries with the subset having CITES records, on a shared 0–250 scale. The overview counts entries with records on a 0–180 scale. A study entry is counted once in each relevant group.

The small coverage bars show entries with records divided by all entries in that risk group. These ratios describe the dataset match, not trade intensity or the share of wild populations being traded.

CITES scope and matching

We use the full CITES Trade Database, version 2026.1, for 2015–2024 and Appendix I–III. Commercial and non-commercial purposes are included, such as research and personal use. A confirmed match requires an unambiguous species identity and at least one positive-quantity source record. Importer and exporter reports are checked; quantities from the two sides are not added.

We found records for 387 study entries. Two further candidates appear only in N-coded records and are outside the Appendix I–III subset. A missing match does not prove no trade. A record alone does not show illegality or establish why a species is threatened.

Annual counts

Each annual square counts distinct study entries with a matched record that year. An entry can occur in several years, so adding annual cells does not give a unique ten-year total. Risk groups use IUCN 2026-1 throughout; they do not reconstruct historical risk assessments.

Counts describe entries, not animals, shipments or trade volume. The full-database snapshot can differ from live queries used in the preceding chapter. The two sources should not be combined as one quantity series.

Product and material examples

The product examples use brand ingredient statements and museum documentation. They identify materials and source species; they are not individual transactions matched in the CITES data. Product information was checked in November 2026 and does not establish sales during 2015–2024.

Bariberry states that its ambergris is beach-cast. CITES Resolution Conf. 9.6 excludes naturally excreted ambergris from the Convention’s provisions. The perfume example therefore does not demonstrate a CITES-controlled transaction.

Yutaka names Japanese eel as 70% of its kabayaki and states that it is farmed and processed in China. The source of its juvenile stock is not given. Japanese eel migrates between freshwater and the sea; no record was matched to it in this study’s CITES extract.

Product images

Yutaka packaging uses the unmodified official transparent image. The perfume bottle was isolated and redrawn from a brand image using an image-generation tool. The earrings are a generated illustration of the material category, not a photograph of a documented object. Third-party product images are used for identification and commentary; rights remain with their owners. No open licence is claimed.

Shared visual foundations

The underwater background and scalloped hammerhead model come from the team’s supplied opening chapter. The background is extended here with local gradients and restrained light. The model by sharkingaround is used under CC BY 4.0.

Scalloped hammerhead model & creator · CC BY 4.0

Local interaction libraries

Chapter motion and text components share one locally bundled GSAP / ScrollTrigger 3.15.1 core, continuing the team’s GSAP-based motion. Context panels use Floating UI for positioning. Decorative side light uses React Bits Side Rays; chapter headings and the closing title use React Bits Blur Text. These components are used under MIT + Commons Clause; React and Motion use MIT licenses; GSAP uses its Standard License. Libraries and notices are bundled locally. The side-light shader is unchanged; a small lifecycle adaptation pauses hidden or inactive canvases.
